Boast

/bōst/ — rhymes with toast · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To boast is to talk proudly, and often at length, about your own achievements or possessions.

He loves to boast about catching the biggest fish at camp.

Worked Example

After winning the chess tournament, Maria spent the entire lunch period boasting about her victory to anyone who would listen, describing every move she'd made.

Boast captures exactly what's happening: she's talking proudly and at length about her achievement in a way that gets annoying. Plain 'brag' is close, but boast specifically includes that sense of going on and on about it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

brag: to talk too proudly about yourself

trumpet: to announce something loudly and proudly

vaunt: to parade your achievements before others boastfully

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

humility: a modest view of your own importance

downplay: to make something seem less impressive

Where it sits · how much someone talks up their success — keep quiet → mention accomplishment → brag → boast

keep quiet vs. boast: Keeping quiet sits at the opposite end of the scale from boast: someone who keeps quiet says nothing about their success, while someone who loves to boast cannot stop talking about it.

mention accomplishment vs. boast: Mentioning an accomplishment is far weaker than boasting: a brief mention states a success once and moves on, while to boast is to dwell on it proudly and at length.

brag vs. boast: Brag is nearly as strong as boast, but boast caps this scale: bragging is loud showing off in the moment, while boasting suggests a proud, ongoing habit of parading your achievements.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — bost

Root — bost: puffed up, swollen with pride (Middle English, probably from a Scandinavian (North Germanic) source)

Put it together

Put it together: The root idea behind boast is being 'puffed up' or swollen with pride. To boast is to let that inflated pride escape as talk — going on and on about your own achievements and possessions.

Use the root in a new word: boastful

Use the root in a new word: boastful: Marco's boastful speech about his three trophies made the audience roll their eyes — boastful is simply boast wearing its adjective ending, describing someone always puffed up with pride.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral to informal

Boast means to talk proudly and at length about your achievements — there's usually an excessive or annoying quality to how much you talk. Use brag for casual talk about your own good qualities; use boast when someone is talking a lot and in a way others find irritating.
